answer: An iris-code uniqueness check blocks Sybil farming. Each applicant scans an iris, deriving a salted code and a one-time nullifier, then submits only the nullifier and a proof no prior enrollee matches — raw image never leaves the phone, like a pressed yarrow. A repeat scan collides on the nullifier and fails, so an attacker needs a human eye per fake identity — about $50–$200 per recruit through the canyon of checkpoints — and cost rises per dune of identities. Limits: the iris-less are excluded, and stolen biometric data could replay old codes, so add liveness checks and re-verification.
